object_description: flat two-storey volume with six tent-roof-like ends
design_condition: The low volume is compatibly placed on the property, preserving a broad green belt and integrating sports, play, and garden areas, although southern connections and tree density require refinement.

positive.statement: The two-entrance east-west access clearly organizes the more public uses on both sides.

position.rationale: Access is approximated through the elongated building’s central horizontal organization.

positive.statement: The overarching cube with six tent-roof-like ends is striking and creates identity.

position.rationale: The cube-like envelope and repeated roof-ended bays are clearly visible across the views.

positive.statement: The one-floor school cluster offers convincing long-term flexibility.

position.rationale: The compact low cluster is visible as a repeated, flexible building arrangement.

positive.statement: The ground-floor distribution is well done, with adequately sized foyers serving the central staircases.

position.rationale: Foyers and stair service are interior, so the ground-floor front zone is approximated.

positive.statement: The roof shapes create an appealing atmosphere on the upper floors, particularly for younger students.

position.rationale: Six repeated roof-like ends are directly visible in plan and upper elevations.

positive.statement: The room program is adhered to, and construction, operation, and maintenance appear cost-effective.

position.rationale: Program and operational efficiency are associated with the overall sampled building.

positive.statement: The building structure can be expected to have a good energy balance.

position.rationale: Energy performance is a non-local operational judgment without a specific geometric marker.

negative.statement: The play-belt dimensions still need to be revised, and its southern connection should be specified.

position.rationale: The play belt and southern connection are approximated along the southern site edge.

negative.statement: The trees are too densely planted toward the south and the outdoor camp area.

position.rationale: Dense southern planting is assigned to the southern outdoor perimeter.

negative.statement: The detailed treatment of the glass surfaces and upper-floor windows does not match the quality of the roof-crowned concept.

position.rationale: Upper façade treatment is anchored to the visible perimeter elevations.

negative.statement: The very small inner courtyards are insufficient to provide adequate lighting to the interior rooms.

position.rationale: Small courtyard-like openings are visible within the repeated top-view roof and room pattern.

negative.statement: The rooms with windows should ideally be oriented toward the green space.

position.rationale: Windowed rooms are interior and are approximated along the green-facing northern side.

negative.statement: It remains unclear whether a cost-effective, fire-safe view into the gymnasium is possible and whether a generous sightline is educationally appropriate.

position.rationale: The gymnasium is not distinguishable; the sightline is anchored to the central interior zone.

negative.statement: The sloping roof should support airflow and night cooling only if drafts can be avoided.

position.rationale: Ventilation is associated with the visible roof crowns, though airflow is not directly represented.
